Synopsis: Asharak has been tasked with getting civilians prepared for war. He hopes having the player on their side might make the difference. If the tiefling leader is dead, Asharak reluctantly steps into his shoes. Off‑screen the player has just come from the wolf‑pens/goblin area and reports that hostile forces are massing in the woods — specifically a drow commander (likely Minthara) who has located the grove. Depending on prior choices the player either escaped and warns Asharak, or has betrayed the grove by leading the drow here; Asharak’s lines shift from grim pragmatism and an offer of joint defense to shocked anger and disbelief if the player admits to siding with the enemy. If the original tiefling leader was killed earlier, Asharak has reluctantly taken up that leadership role and is scrambling to prepare civilians now. - GOB_DrowAndCaptured_ThreeWayDialog.json: You and your party have been brought before Nightwarden Minthara in the goblin camp, escorted by a captured goblin (Sazza) you recovered from a nearby druid grove. retrieved_synopses: Asharak is the tiefling organizer charged with readying civilians of the grove for an imminent attack; he’s relieved and surprised to see the player because he’d assumed they’d died at the goblin camp. Off‑screen the player has just come from the wolf‑pens/goblin area and reports that hostile forces are massing in the woods — specifically a drow commander (likely Minthara) who has located the grove. Depending on prior choices the player either escaped and warns Asharak, or has betrayed the grove by leading the drow here; Asharak’s lines shift from grim pragmatism and an offer of joint defense to shocked anger and disbelief if the player admits to siding with the enemy. If the original tiefling leader was killed earlier, Asharak has reluctantly taken up that leadership role and is scrambling to prepare civilians now.

You and your party have been brought before Nightwarden Minthara in the goblin camp, escorted by a captured goblin (Sazza) you recovered from a nearby druid grove. Minthara wields authority and can probe minds; she learns the grove’s location from the goblin and intends to raid it, demanding the player’s cooperation — either by opening the gate and signalling the assault or by refusing and fighting her. The goblin’s fate hinges on whether she (or Minthara) recognises the player as a True Soul: if she does, Minthara will spare the prisoner; if not, Minthara will execute her unless you intervene. Off‑screen events in the camp (recent fights in the wolf pens, a druid/bear presence, and other encounters with goblin leadership) help explain the tension and the stakes but aren’t spelled out in these lines.

the drow commander and goblins arrive during the attack on the grove to find the player has already gone hostile to the tieflings by attacking them. The drow is amused that the player would start the slaughter without her and either joins them to finish off the tieflings, or gives futher orders if all are dead

You’re speaking with a grove resident (Apikusis) just after the Emerald Grove has been attacked and the player helped drive out a goblin assault. The scene can reflect two states: the immediate aftermath of repelling the raid, or the later moment after goblin leaders have been killed and the tieflings are leaving the grove; in either case the grove is damaged and people are preparing a long recovery. Apikusis thanks the player for saving a sacred place, expresses cautious hope, and acknowledges the hard work ahead to make things whole again. If the grove’s idol was taken earlier in your playthrough, an extra response will note that the idol is missing and the grove feels exposed. Off‑screen events from the Wolf Pens cluster (combat, the druid/animal presence, and decisions about goblin leadership) may have shaped how tense or sanguine she sounds.

Takes place immediately after the player blows the horn at the gates of the grove, beginning an attack on the refugees hiding there. The surviving tiefling leader rallies his troops, then the drow commander arrives with her retinue of goblins. She mind-melds with the player. She expects them - as True Souls - to betray the tieflings, and players must choose whether to side with her OR with the tieflings as the attack begins.

This is a huge fight and a decisive moment for the tieflings, the drow/goblins, AND the players.
context: Asharak is the tiefling organizer tasked with readying the civilians of the grove for an imminent raid and has been scrambling to prepare them for battle. Off‑screen the player has just come from the goblin/wolf‑pens area and reports that hostile forces are massing in the woods — specifically a drow commander (likely Minthara) who now knows the grove’s location. Depending on prior choices, the player either escaped the camp and returns to warn Asharak, or betrayed the grove by guiding the drow to it; Asharak’s lines shift from relieved pragmatism to shocked anger in response. If the original tiefling leader was killed earlier, Asharak has reluctantly assumed that leadership role and is trying to rally frightened civilians for the coming fight.
